fieldMarks: Alternating longitudinal dark brown and tan stripes from nape to tail base, the 'thirteen lines'
Dark stripes broader, with tan rectangular spots along the midline
Total length 225-300 mm; tail 75-109 mm, thin and sparingly bushy
behavior: Emerges from hibernation March or early April; enters by October, adults from July
Prefers loosely constituted family groups but is not colonial
Eats seeds, fruit, grasses, forbs and insects; sometimes small vertebrates
habitat: Dry, sandy or 'tighter' soils in open areas: grasslands, meadows, cultivated fields, roadsides, airfields, shrublands, lawns and golf courses; avoids woods.
range: South-central Canada to Texas, and from Montana, Wyoming, Utah and eastern Arizona to Michigan, Ohio, Missouri and Oklahoma.
